get.description: Per-pool **price-impact / slippage** — "how much SOL to move price N%" and the impact + tokens received for each buy size. For every pool: `spot_price_sol`, `quotes[]` per requested SOL size (`tokens_out`, `avg_price_sol`, `price_impact_pct`), and `to_move_price` (SOL to move price 1%/5%/10%). Exact for constant-product AMMs (PumpSwap, Raydium v4/CPMM, Meteora DAMM — served from streamed reserves, `source: "stream"`); pump.fun bonding curves priced from one live read of the curve's virtual reserves (`source: "live_rpc"`). Raydium LaunchLab (bonk / LetsBonk) curves return under `unsupported_pools[]` with `reason: "launchlab_fee_basis_unproven"` (since 2026-10-27: they were priced on the virtual reserves alone with a flat 100 bps fee, while the program trades on virtual minus real base and virtual plus real quote and charges a protocol fee plus a per-platform fee). Impact is per-pool, not router-optimal; concentrated-liquidity pools (Raydium CLMM, Orca, Meteora DLMM) and unclassified pools return under `unsupported_pools[]` with a `reason` instead of a wrong number. **Concentrated depth models (rollout behind server flags, off by default):** when enabled, Meteora DLMM pools are quoted with the program's own integer bin math from one same-slot snapshot of the pair and a bounded bin-array window (`model: "concentrated"`, `model_detail: "meteora_dlmm_bins"`, `fee_basis: "dynamic_fee_at_quote_time"`, `bins_window`), at most 3 DLMM pools per request; Raydium CLMM pools likewise with the program's own integer tick math (Q64.64 sqrt price, tick arrays, AmmConfig trade fee) from one same-slot snapshot of the pool, its config and the tick arrays in the buy direction (`model_detail: "raydium_clmm_ticks"`, `fee_basis: "amm_config_at_quote_time"`, `ticks_window`), at most 3 CLMM pools per request; Meteora DAMM v2 pools get a number only when their Pool account is proven and full-range (`model_detail: "meteora_damm_v2_full_range"`, `pool_account`, fee = the venue default, not the pool's own fee schedule), otherwise they return under `unsupported_pools[]` with a `damm_v2_*` reason, never a generic constant-product number; a size that would cross past the loaded ticks has `status: "exceeds_loaded_ticks"`; every quote then carries a `status`, and a size the loaded window cannot fill has `status: "exceeds_loaded_bins"` with null numbers (never a constant-product fallback). The response then also carries `pool_selection` (largest known pool vs the pool depth is reported for; `routing: "single_pool_only"`, multi-pool routing is not computed). PRO+.

parameters.name: sizes
parameters.description: Comma-separated SOL buy sizes to quote (max 8, each >0 and ≤10000). Default 0.5,1,5,10.

found.description: false = no depth-computable pool (pools may still appear in unsupported_pools)

model.description: constant_product | curve | concentrated (concentrated only with a concentrated depth model enabled)

model_detail.description: Which program-exact model produced the numbers: concentrated pools (DLMM bins, CLMM ticks), or meteora_damm_v2_full_range = a Meteora DAMM v2 pool whose Pool account is proven (owner, layout, vault) and full-range, quoted constant-product (Meteora DAMM v2 model enabled).

pool_account.description: Meteora DAMM v2 only (model_detail meteora_damm_v2_full_range): the proven DAMM v2 Pool account. pool_address is the token vault.

fee_pct.description: Swap fee, %. Meteora DLMM: base + variable fee at quote time (fee_basis).

fee_basis.description: observed_event = PumpSwap fee observed on the pool's swap events (virtual-reserve model); dynamic_fee_at_quote_time = Meteora DLMM base + variable fee with the reference decayed to the quote time; amm_config_at_quote_time = Raydium CLMM trade fee read from the pool's AmmConfig in the same snapshot. Absent = the venue's static fee.

bins_window.description: Meteora DLMM only: the bin range loaded in the snapshot and its slot. Quotes never walk outside it.

ticks_window.description: Raydium CLMM only: the loaded tick range [from_tick, to_tick) in the buy direction (the current tick array plus 4) and its slot. Quotes never cross a tick outside it.

status.description: Concentrated models only. filled = fully quoted; pool_liquidity_exhausted = the pool's own liquidity range ends first (partial fill reported); exceeds_loaded_bins (DLMM) / exceeds_loaded_ticks (CLMM) = the size needs liquidity outside the loaded window (numbers null); price_out_of_range = the program's price math is undefined there (numbers null).

available.description: Concentrated models only. true = the whole size fills inside the loaded window with output > 0; false = this size has no usable quote (see status). A pool is listed here only when at least one requested size is available; a concentrated pool where no size is available is under unsupported_pools[] (dlmm_insufficient_liquidity_in_loaded_bins / clmm_insufficient_liquidity_in_loaded_ticks).

fillable_up_to_sol.description: Meteora DLMM, unavailable sizes only: SOL input (incl. fees) the loaded bins can absorb before the walk stops. null when available.

tokens_out.description: null when status is exceeds_loaded_bins or price_out_of_range

1pct.description: SOL to move price +1% (null on a concentrated pool when the loaded window does not reach that price, or when no liquidity lies between the current and the target price: a move is never reported as costing 0)

universe.description: Only the deepest max_pools pools by stored liquidity are evaluated (audit F19); pools past that cut are not listed. truncated=true = the cut dropped pools.

fillable_up_to_sol.description: With reason dlmm_insufficient_liquidity_in_loaded_bins: the largest SOL input (incl. fees) the loaded bins can absorb (0 = no buy-side liquidity in the window).

reason.description: e.g. concentrated_liquidity_depth_not_supported, pool_model_unknown, curve_graduated_use_amm_pool, reserves_unavailable. With the Meteora DLMM model enabled also: dlmm_lb_pair_unknown, dlmm_lb_pair_not_found, dlmm_lb_pair_unreadable, dlmm_pair_disabled, dlmm_rpc_unavailable, dlmm_not_evaluated_pool_budget (past the per-request pool budget), dlmm_depth_uncomputable, dlmm_insufficient_liquidity_in_loaded_bins (no requested size fills inside the loaded bin window, e.g. a one-sided or drained pair; carries fillable_up_to_sol and bins_window), dlmm_active_bin_not_loaded, dlmm_bin_array_unreadable, dlmm_bin_array_mismatch, dlmm_bin_array_window_gap, dlmm_no_bin_arrays, dlmm_snapshot_invalid, pool_mint_mismatch, exotic_quote_depth_not_supported, token_mint_unreadable, token2022_transfer_fee_not_modeled, sol_usd_unavailable_for_stable_quote. With the Raydium CLMM model enabled also: clmm_pool_state_unknown, clmm_pool_not_found (the stored pool is not a Raydium CLMM account), clmm_pool_unreadable, clmm_config_unreadable, clmm_config_mismatch, clmm_swap_disabled, clmm_pool_not_open, clmm_unknown_pool_extension, clmm_rpc_unavailable, clmm_not_evaluated_pool_budget, clmm_depth_uncomputable, clmm_insufficient_liquidity_in_loaded_ticks (no requested size fills inside the loaded tick window; carries ticks_window), clmm_current_tick_not_loaded, clmm_tick_price_mismatch, clmm_tick_array_missing, clmm_tick_array_unreadable, clmm_tick_array_mismatch, clmm_tick_array_window_gap, clmm_tick_index_mismatch, clmm_tick_bitmap_mismatch, clmm_liquidity_negative, clmm_snapshot_invalid. Shared concentrated-depth budget (DLMM + CLMM together): concentrated_depth_busy (process-wide concurrent snapshot limit reached), concentrated_depth_budget_exhausted (per-minute RPC budget reached). With the Meteora DAMM v2 model enabled (rows under the DAMM v2 vault authority, whatever their dex label): damm_v2_pool_unknown (no proven Pool account stored), damm_v2_pool_unavailable (live read failed), damm_v2_pool_not_found, damm_v2_pool_wrong_owner, damm_v2_unknown_layout, damm_v2_pool_vault_mismatch, damm_v2_single_range (proven but concentrated price range; no depth model yet)

pool_selection.description: Only with a concentrated depth model enabled. Which pool is the largest we know of vs the pool depth is reported for; multi-pool routing is not computed or promised.

largest_known_pool.description: Largest evaluated pool by stored liquidity, supported or not.

largest_known_pool_supported.description: false = the largest known pool is in unsupported_pools; the primary pool is a smaller one.

primary_pool.description: Deepest pool with depth available (same as the top-level primary_pool).

post.summary: Batch token risk scoring (up to 50 mints)
post.description: Same loader and per-mint shape as `GET /tokens/{mint}/risk` (score v2, assessment, dev block, coverage) for up to 50 mints — identical evidence gives identical scores. Documented difference: no live dev-holdings RPC per mint, so `dev.holdings_*` are null and `dev.transfer_status` is `unknown` (the dev block never moves the score). Untracked mints come back as `{ mint, error: "not_tracked" }`, and mints whose score-critical inputs could not be read as `{ mint, error: "unavailable", retryable: true }` — never a partial score. PRO+.

band.description: Never `safe` while assessment.status is `incomplete`, or with an un-revoked mint/freeze authority

score_version.description: v2.1 scores measured primary-pool LP shares. v2 uses the legacy LP status when no eligible measurement is available.

status.description: ok/warn/danger = evidence read and scored. unknown = the input should exist but could not be read or is insufficient (0 points; listed in assessment.unknown_inputs; band never safe). not_assessed = no evidence source applies to this token (0 points; listed in assessment.not_assessed). Neither is ever positive evidence.

inputs.description: Every scorer input. Enrichment fields are null when unobserved — unknown, not false/0.

token_supply_burn_detected.description: The mint's supply decreased (token burn). Not LP evidence.

lp_burn_status.description: LP burn/lock evidence: `verified` only with measured LP-token custody (lp_burnt_pct ≥ 99). No Solana writer populates LP custody yet, so today every token is `unknown`. A token-supply burn is never promoted to an LP claim.

lp_shares.description: Measured shares of the primary pool LP ledger at observed_at, truncated to four decimal places.

deployer_history_status.description: null when there is no deployer

deployer_reputation_scored.description: Whether the bonding rate moved the score (established history only)

liquidity_observed_at.description: When the liquidity figure was last observed (mc-tracker last trade). With the creator not assessed, band safe requires this within the last 6 h (null or more than 5 min in the future = not fresh). 6 h is a policy threshold, not proof that the liquidity is still there.

status.description: incomplete = at least one score input is unknown; the score is a lower bound

unknown_inputs.description: Inputs not observed for this token (e.g. transfer_fee, mint_authority, liquidity, kol_activity, deployer_reputation, blacklist, supply_inflation, launch_cohort). deployer_reputation is unknown when a creator lookup failed, when a LAUNCHPAD mint's creator was not recorded (a coverage gap), or when a known creator has no established history.

explanations.description: Why each unknown / not-assessed input is listed, keyed by input name, plus band_cap when the band was capped (creator not assessed and liquidity / liquidity-to-MC not both ok, or the liquidity figure older than 6 h — a policy threshold, not proof of safety). Missing required creator information never yields band safe, for any token.

not_assessed.description: Dimensions not measured for this token that are NOT a failed lookup: lp_custody (never observed for Solana pools) and deployer_reputation only when the token has no launchpad origin in our capture (no deploy row, no bonding-curve pool, not PumpSwap-primary, no pump/bonk/BAGS vanity suffix). A launchpad mint with an unrecorded creator, or a failed origin lookup, is an unknown input instead.

dev_status.description: ok = dev block present · not_found = no pending_deploys row (not a launchpad deploy we saw) · unavailable = the lookup failed

dev.description: Dev-wallet activity (migration 225). Trade-derived fields are accurate THROUGH activity_rollup_through; holdings are observed at holdings_observed_at — never at as_of.

holdings_tokens.description: Live on-chain balance (60 s cache); null = RPC unavailable or not checked (batch)

holdings_observed_at.description: When the RPC balance was observed (cache fetch time)

activity_rollup_through.description: Dev trades are rolled up through this time (dev_activity cursor)

expected_tokens_from_trades.description: Balance the dev's own recorded trades explain, aligned to holdings_observed_at

transfer_status.description: suspected = balance below what recorded trades explain (a sell on an uncaptured venue looks identical) — never a verified transfer; unknown = observations misaligned, rollup stale, no coverage, or holdings not checked

transferred_out.description: DEPRECATED boolean view of transfer_status: true = suspected, false = none_detected, null = unknown

as_of.description: Response time — not the observation time of any input

error.description: Present instead of a score: not_tracked = no snapshot data; unavailable = a score-critical input could not be read (retryable: true, unavailable_inputs lists them) — never a partial score; error = the per-mint compute failed (retryable when it was a statement timeout)

post.summary: Recent trades for up to 50 wallets in one call
post.description:
The batch twin of `GET /wallet/{address}/trades`: same rows, same fields, same 90-day window — for **up to 50 wallets per request**, up to 100 trades each, newest first. Pass `since` (unix seconds) and you get only trades newer than that across every wallet; the response's `next_since` is the newest `block_time` seen, so feed it straight back on the next poll. Missing wallets come back with an empty `trades` array — *not observed*, never a 404.

**Why:** sweeping many wallets through the single-wallet route costs one request per wallet; fifty lookups in one call is one round-trip and one quota unit. Trades carry `price_sol`/`price_usd` (executed) and `market_price_sol`/`market_price_usd` (canonical) exactly like the single route.

**Coverage honesty:** the tape is the pump.fun / LaunchLab / bags pipeline — a wallet's Raydium-native or Meteora memecoin trades are not on it; the `coverage` block says so. PRO+.

wallets.description: Base58 wallet addresses. Also accepts a comma-separated string.

since.description: Unix seconds; only trades strictly after this. Default: 90 days ago (cannot reach further back).

market_price_sol.description: Canonical pool price sampled near this trade's slot

next_since.description: Newest block_time seen — feed back as `since` on the next poll

post.summary: Batch wallet reputation flags (up to 100 addresses)
post.description:
Bulk reputation classification: `is_sniper`, `is_bundler`, `is_dumper` (+ raw dump-cluster cohort counts), `is_kol`, and `bot_confidence` for up to 100 wallets in one call. Flag values match the `flags` block on `GET /wallet/{address}` exactly.

**Semantics**: flags derive from the pump.fun trade pipeline — `false` means "not observed", not "verified clean". `is_sniper` is behavior-updated (hourly); `is_bundler` is a lifetime flag; `is_dumper` uses a rolling 42-day window recomputed daily. PRO+.

label_coverage.description: Whether each flag's rule actually evaluated this wallet. evaluated=false → the boolean is 'no evidence', not 'verified clean'.

post.description:
Enterprise only. Scores an arbitrary, customer-supplied list of Solana wallets on real FIFO cost-basis trading performance — not membership in our pre-tracked KOL/alpha lists (any wallet works, same as `GET /wallet/{address}/pnl`). Each wallet gets a transparent 0-100 `score` (50% win rate on closed positions + 50% profit factor, capped 5x — see `score_methodology` in the response), the full PnL summary, and the same reputation flags as `/wallet/batch/classify`.

**Live-compute cap**: PnL is the expensive half of `/pnl` (up to 50k paginated trades + FIFO). Up to 200 wallets per call, but only the first 25 UNCACHED wallets are computed inline per request — the rest come back `status: "not_computed"`. Cached wallets (recently scored, or recently looked up via `/wallet/{address}/pnl`) are always free regardless of the cap. Resubmit a `not_computed` address alone, or call again shortly, to pick up its score once warm.

score.description: 0-100. null when there are no closed positions to score (open-only, no_trades, or not_computed).

pnl.description: Same shape as GET /wallet/{address}/pnl's `summary` block. null unless status is "scored".

cache_age_seconds.description: Seconds since computed_at (source age survives a cache hit)

400.description: Invalid body — not an array of 1-200 base58 addresses

403.description: Requires the Enterprise contract tier (hand-sold — see /pricing#enterprise)

get.description: Per-wallet activity stats for every Solana wallet you've added to your tracker. Capacity: PRO 50, ULTRA 250, BUSINESS 1,000 wallets. BASIC has no access to the wallet tracker (403).

parameters.name: wallet
parameters.description: Restrict to one tracked wallet (base58).

get.description:
Aggregate counters for any Solana wallet over the last 90 days plus cross-product flags joining `kol_wallets`, `mv_alpha_wallets` (incl. bot_confidence), `deployers`, and the reputation caches (`is_sniper`, `is_bundler`, `is_dumper` + dump-cluster cohort counts). Backed by `idx_token_trades_wallet_cover` — sub-100ms even on heavy wallets. Returns 404 if the wallet has no trades AND no flag-table presence.

**v1.8.1 enrichments** (additive, non-breaking): also returns `top_tokens` (top-traded tokens with realized PnL + peak MC), `trading_style` (avg trade size, sniper-rate, round-trip rate, median hold), `deployer_breakdown` (tier-distribution of deployers bought from), and `recent_trades` (last 10 trades with symbols). PRO+.

get.summary: FIFO cost-basis PnL with daily curve
get.description:
Full per-wallet PnL: realized + unrealized SOL, profit factor, max drawdown, avg + median hold minutes, daily UTC PnL curve, closed positions sorted by pnl desc (with ROI %, hold minutes, win/loss/breakeven), and open positions hydrated with current prices from market-cap tracker.

**Caching**: stored in `wallet_analyses` with dynamic TTL — 5 min for wallets active in last 24h, 1h for 1-7d old, 24h for dormant. Every hit is validated against the wallet's trade head (audit F16): a wallet that traded after the cached analysis is recomputed (`cache_invalidated: new_activity`), so a resumed dormant wallet never gets a day-old answer. `cache_age_seconds` + `computed_at` carry the source age on a hit. Cache hits don't count against your daily quota.

**Honesty note**: two limits, both disclosed in the response. (1) Time — cost basis is only observable inside our 90-day data window, and capture itself starts 2026-04-12; a wallet that sold tokens bought before that has the overflow silently discarded rather than fabricated (`notes.cost_basis_observable_from` surfaces the cutoff). (2) Token universe — persisted trades are gated to the launchpad pipeline (pump.fun, LaunchLab/bonk, bags), so a wallet trading outside it is not partially covered but uncovered. The `coverage` object reports `in_scope`; when it is false, zero and empty results mean 'not captured', not 'no activity'. PRO+.

404.description: Wallet has no trades in the data window

get.description: Open lots only — same data as `/pnl` `open_positions[]` but without the summary, curve, or closed-positions payload. Shares the `wallet_analyses` cache: if you've recently called `/pnl` for this wallet, this call is an immediate cache hit. PRO+.

completeness.description: Realized-PnL completeness. incomplete when at least one sell in the response has proceeds that went to another wallet (price_status proceeds_unattributed, migration 508): realized PnL and ROI then cover the known basis only, and the basis those sells consumed is reported as unknown_realized_cost_basis_sol, never as 0 proceeds or a loss. This is realized-PnL completeness. It is NOT `coverage.completeness` (source-coverage verification: verified / not_verified / ...), which says whether the trade capture for this subject is proven complete.

incomplete_reasons.description: Empty when complete. /wallet/{address} emits only proceeds_unattributed; /tokens/{mint}/top-traders emits proceeds_unattributed and, since migration 548 (2026-11-11), unknown_consideration; unknown_consideration and missing_cost_basis (sales without an observed purchase) are shared with the FIFO routes (/pnl, /positions).

summary.description: Realized-PnL completeness of the wallet (same values as /pnl summary).

unknown_realized_cost_basis_sol.description: Migration 508: cost basis consumed by sells whose proceeds went to another wallet. NOT in realized_pnl_sol or ROI (neither a loss nor a gain). 0 when complete.

holding_check.description: COV-21: summary of the proven-holding check over the returned open positions (SOLANA_POSITION_HOLDING; mode off = every position unverified/not_checked).

cache_age_seconds.description: Cache hits only — seconds since computed_at

cache_validation.description: Cache hits only (audit F16): head_checked = the wallet has no persisted trade newer than the analysis watermark, so the cached analysis is current; unverified = the trade-head probe failed and the unexpired cache was served flagged. A hit whose wallet traded after the watermark is never served — it is recomputed.

cache_invalidated.description: Present on a recompute that happened because a cached analysis existed but the wallet traded after it

get.description: The wallet's ACTUAL current token balances, read live from chain (SPL + Token-2022 accounts + SOL balance), then enriched from our data (price, market cap, name/symbol). Unlike `/positions` (trade-derived FIFO — transfer-blind, launchpad-scoped), this is a chain-verified holdings census. Each holding carries `transfer_delta` = on-chain amount minus the trade-derived net position, which exposes tokens that arrived/left WITHOUT a swap (airdrops, insider funding, wallet-hopping). 90s cache; 6 uncached lookups/min/user. ULTRA only.

coverage.description: Disambiguates trade_derived_amount:null — in_scope:false means the WALLET has no captured trades at all, so every null is a coverage gap, not a transfer signal.

503.description: Temporarily too heavy — either the upstream RPC is busy or the wallet holds too many tokens to aggregate right now. Retry shortly (retry_after_seconds).

get.summary: Paginated raw trades for any wallet
get.description:
Cursor-paginated `token_trades` rows for the wallet (launchpad-pipeline mints only). Trades stored from 2026-10-22T19:53:00.000Z have no size floor. Before 2026-10-22T19:53:00.000Z (legacy policy) buys under 0.05 SOL (under $3.50 when paid in USDC/USDT) were not stored; sells that receive SOL were kept at any size. The market-cap band (min_mc_usd / max_mc_usd) is applied BEFORE limit and cursor (since 2026-10-05): limit=N returns up to N matching signals, and paging with cursor= (the next_cursor of the previous page) neither skips nor repeats matches. get.description: Live health of the 7 core services (KOL tracker, deployer listener, API server, database, WebSocket, plus Robinhood Chain node sync and trade-ingest freshness), 24h/7d uptime, and data-quality measures (accuracy, correctness, drift, serve-time). Per-service `status` is one of `healthy` | `degraded` | `down` | `stale` | `unknown` — `stale` means the monitor itself has not reported within 3x its 5-minute cadence (the last row's claim is unverifiable; `reported_status` carries what it said), `unknown` means no check row exists at all. Top-level `status` is computed over ALL 7 core services: `incident` if any is down, `degraded` if any is degraded/stale/unknown, `operational` only when every service has a fresh healthy check. `slo_target_pct` is an operating TARGET, not a measured result or a contractual guarantee. Public — no auth required.

post.description:
Returns your stream token plus the WebSocket URL for the realtime stream. **The token does not expire** (since 2026-08-27): one token per user, the same value on every call, so multi-process clients can each call this at boot and nothing ever needs refreshing. It stops working only when the subscription lapses, or when you send `{"rotate": true}` in the body to replace it (the previous value keeps working for 60 s). `expires_at` / `next_refresh_at` are always `null` and kept only for wire compatibility. Present the token as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on the handshake (preferred) or `?token=` — it is masked in our access logs either way. ULTRA and BUSINESS responses also include `dex_ws_url` for the DEX firehose. PRO/ULTRA only.

After connecting, send `{"type":"subscribe","channels":[...]}` — nothing is delivered until you subscribe. Channels: `kol:trades`, `kol:coordination` (PRO+, user-scoped: fires of your own /kol/coordination/alerts rules), `kol:first_touches` (PRO+), `deployer:alerts`, `wallet_tracker:events` (ULTRA, subscriber-scoped), `copytrade:signals` (PRO+, user-scoped), `price_alert:events` (PRO+, user-scoped), `sniper:deploys` (ULTRA/BUSINESS/ENTERPRISE), `token:graduations` (PRO+ — every pump.fun graduation, tracked deployer or not), `token:prices` (PRO+, **mint-scoped**: `filters.mints` is required and capped per connection at 25 PRO / 100 ULTRA / 250 BUSINESS — a subscribe above the cap is rejected, never truncated; ~250 ms coalesced ticks, event `token:price`), `token:locks` (PRO+ — new Streamflow / Jupiter Lock / Bonfida lock or vesting contracts), `token:fee_claims` (PRO+ — pump.fun creator-fee distributions, social-handle claims and config changes), `token:surges` (PRO+ — token momentum fires: events `token:surge` for new tokens running vs their launch MC, tiers early/strong/breakout, and `token:revival` for ≥24 h-dormant tokens confirmed trading again; subscribe filters `kinds[]`, `tiers[]`, `launchpads[]`, `exclude_flags[]`, `min_mc_usd`/`max_mc_usd`, `deployer_tier[]`), and for **Robinhood Chain** `rhc:kol_trades` (PRO+), `rhc:dex_trades` (ULTRA+), `rhc:dex_trades_unattributed` (ULTRA+ — the additive complement to `rhc:dex_trades`: trades on a pool where no single side could be classified as the token, either because both sides are recognized quote/equity-quote assets like WETH/USDG, or, rarer, because neither is. Fully present in `rhc_trades` but omitted from `rhc:dex_trades`; subscribe to both for full chain coverage. Raw leg data only — `token_in`/`token_out`/`amount_in`/`amount_out`, no decimals/symbol enrichment, no buy/sell `action`), `rhc:new_tokens` (ULTRA+, one event per token the moment its symbol/name/decimals first resolve on chain, before its first trade), `rhc:copytrade:signals` (PRO+, user-scoped), `rhc:price_alert:events` (PRO+, user-scoped), `rhc:kol:coordination` (PRO+, user-scoped), `rhc:kol:first_touches` (PRO+, broadcast — ULTRA is required for the first-touch *subscription* endpoint, not for this channel) , `rhc:token_locks` (PRO+, broadcast: one event per token lock or vesting contract created on chain; withdrawals are not tracked) and `rhc:token_prices` (PRO+, **address-scoped**: `filters.addresses` is required and capped per connection at 25 PRO / 100 ULTRA / 250 BUSINESS (counted across named subscriptions), rejected above the cap, never truncated; event `rhc:token_price`: one snapshot per address on subscribe (`snapshot: true`, from the current price row), then ticks derived from the RHC trade feed at most once per address per 250 ms with the latest value, each carrying `quality` fresh | stale | unreliable and `quality_reason` (no_price, dust_trade, curve_live, state_quote_fallback, low_liquidity, price_age, mc_ceiling), `price_source`, `source_pool`, `liquidity_usd`, `observed_at`, `price_age_ms`; a stale or unreliable price is never delivered as fresh; state stream with no seq/id, a resume gets a fresh snapshot; under a named subscription every frame carries `sub_id`), `rhc:lp_events` (ULTRA+, RHC liquidity events: add / remove / pool_created on tracked Uniswap v2/v3/v4 pools with in_range + share + material; filters addresses, pools, dexes, actions, material_only, min_share), and the Phase 4 scoped channels, all PRO+ and all capped per connection at 25 PRO / 100 ULTRA / 250 BUSINESS tokens or wallets, each channel its own budget, rejected above the cap and never truncated: `token:candles` (**mint-scoped**, `filters.mints` required: live 1-minute candles, the stored row when the minute closes, optional in-progress minute with `filters.updates: true`), `rhc:token_candles` (**address-scoped**, `filters.addresses` required: the same for Robinhood Chain, plus revisions of a rewritten candle), `token:risk` (**mint-scoped**: risk-INPUT changes, mint or freeze authority revoked, transfer fee changed, first supply-inflation crossing; not a risk band or score stream), `rhc:token_risk` (**address-scoped**: a stored RHC risk verdict that changed at a sweep recheck), `wallet:scores` (**wallet-scoped**, `filters.wallets` required: deployer tier changes and KOL categorical state changes) and `rhc:wallet_scores` (**wallet-scoped**, `filters.wallets` with 0x addresses: RHC deployer tier changes). `rhc:dev_activity` (ULTRA+): the recorded developer of an RHC token buying or selling it (dev_buy / dev_sell only, never transfers; filters types / addresses / deployers / action; ring replay only); live since 2026-10-05. `token:bundles` / `rhc:token_bundles` (PRO+, broadcast), rhc:token_holders (PRO+, address-scoped holder state: snapshot, then changed balances per fold), token:holders_top (PRO+, mint-scoped, filters.mints REQUIRED: the Solana holder index top holders per mint, depth PRO 10 / ULTRA 50 / BUSINESS 100), token:trades (PRO+, mint-scoped, filters.mints REQUIRED: committed Solana trades, each frame the exact GET /tokens/{mint}/trades row, live from subscribe): one `token:bundle_cluster` / `rhc:token_bundle_cluster` per NEW coordinated buy cluster on any token, launch or later (3+ distinct buyers in one slot / block, 3+ of them new to the token); durable resume; optional filters `mints` / `addresses`, `min_wallets`, `min_new_wallets`, `phases`, `atomic_only`. For the share of supply these wallets hold now, call `/tokens/{mint}/bundle-share` / `/rhc/tokens/{address}/bundle-share`. `rhc:dex_trade` / `rhc:dex_trade_unattributed` payloads carry additive enrichment since 2026-09-22: `amount_in_raw` / `amount_out_raw` as exact decimal strings (never floats), `token` + `quote` {address, symbol, decimals} (`token_in_meta` / `token_out_meta` on the unattributed channel), `metadata_status` known | pending | unknown, `price_status` fresh | stale | none with `price_source` and `price_observed_at`, `mc_status` (why `mc_usd` is null), `side` buy | sell only when a canonical quote defines the token, else null with `side_reason`; a KOL trade appears on both `rhc:kol_trades` and `rhc:dex_trades` with the same `tx_hash` + `log_index` and different ids. **36 channels total** (19 Solana + 17 Robinhood Chain; the registry is `services/shared/stream-channels.mjs` and the `connected` frame echoes it). `rhc:trades` is accepted as a deprecated alias of `rhc:dex_trades` (older RHC SDKs sent it) — new code should subscribe to `rhc:dex_trades`. RHC channels ride the SAME socket and the same connection limit as the Solana channels — no second connection needed — but carry EVM-native fields (lowercase `0x` addresses, `eth_amount`, `tx_hash`, `block_number`), so do not reuse a Solana deserializer unchanged.

**Liquidity and lock lifecycle (Phase 3, 2026-09-23).** `rhc:lp_events` delivers event `rhc:lp_event` (id `rhc:lp_event:<tx_hash>:<log_index>`) with `action` add | remove | pool_created, raw `amount0`/`amount1` strings (null on v4, whose ModifyLiquidity reports no token amounts), the position range, `in_range`, `active_liquidity_delta`, `active_share` / `active_share_reason`, `share_of_reserves` (v2) and `material` (a removal of at least 25 % of reserves or active liquidity). `in_range` and the active fields are null (`pool_state_unknown`) when the pool's current tick was not known, never guessed; `provider` is usually a router or position manager, not the beneficial owner; there is no USD field. Invalid lp filters reject the channel rather than widening it. Durable resume from storage (up to 10,000 rows). On `token:locks` and `rhc:token_locks`, `filters.lifecycle: true` opts a subscription into lifecycle events (without it the channel is unchanged): Solana `token:lock_claimed`, `token:lock_cancelled`, `token:lock_closed`, `token:lock_updated` (change topup | extended | schedule_changed | recipient_changed), `token:unlock_upcoming` (next unlock within 24 h) and `token:unlock_available` (the unlock passed within 30 min: claimable per the schedule, NOT claimed); Robinhood Chain `rhc:token_unlock_upcoming` / `rhc:token_unlock_available` only, because RHC claims, extensions and cancels are not observable (`withdrawals_tracked: false`). Further lifecycle filters: `events[]`, `unlock_kinds[]` (cliff, period, final, tranche), `include_automatic_claims` (default false: Streamflow keeper-cranked withdrawals, about 90 % of claim volume, are hidden unless set), and `mints` (Solana) / `addresses` (RHC). Ids are `<event>:<event_key>`, deduplicated durably server-side, and no event is emitted for history (backfills and reconciliation never alert).

**Candles, risk inputs and wallet scores (Phase 4, 2026-09-23).** All six channels are scoped only (no firehose on any tier). The cap counts the union across every named subscription on the connection, and each channel has its OWN budget: one PRO socket may watch 25 price mints, 25 candle mints and 25 risk mints at once. A missing or empty scope, a malformed entry or a scope above the cap rejects the channel (`channels_rejected`; codes `candles_missing_filter`, `candles_invalid_scope`, `candles_over_cap`, `candles_invalid_filters`, `risk_scope_missing`, `risk_scope_invalid`, `risk_scope_over_cap`, `risk_invalid_filters`, `wallet_scores_missing_filter`, `wallet_scores_invalid_filter`, `wallet_scores_over_cap`), an `update` that would make it invalid is refused whole (`invalid_filters`), and a downgrade above the new cap revokes it (`channels_revoked`). The generic filter keys (`action`, `min_mc_usd`, ...) never apply to these events. Their events enter the in-memory replay buffer only while a connected subscription watches the token or wallet, so a resume of a subscription holding them is served from storage; put them in their own named subscription. None of these event types can be registered as a webhook.

**Candles.** Events `candle:closed` (Solana) and `rhc:candle_closed` / `rhc:candle_revised` (RHC) carry the stored 1-minute row (`bucket_start`, `bucket_end`, `closed_at`, open/high/low/close price and MC, liquidity, supply, volumes, `trades`, buy/sell counts, `dex`, `pool_address`, `final: true`, `source`; RHC adds `revision` / `revised_at`). Id `candle:<chain>:<token>:<bucket_start epoch s>`, a revision appends `:r<n>`. With `filters.updates: true` the channel also sends `candle:update` / `rhc:candle_update`: the producer's in-progress minute, at most one per token per second, a state stream with no seq/id that is never replayed (`replay_end.channels.<ch>.updates` says `mode: none`, `gap: state_stream`), and with no snapshot of the open candle on subscribe (the first update comes with the next price move). A fully flat candle with no trades (o = h = l = c, 0 trades) is not emitted live and not replayed. Solana has no revised event: a rare merged rewrite of a minute is published under the same id as the first close. RHC replays only the latest revision of a candle. Frames arrive up to about 25 s after the minute ends. Durable resume from the candle tables for the subscription's tokens only, up to 10,000 rows.

**Risk inputs.** `token:risk` events `risk:authority_changed` (field `mint_authority` | `freeze_authority` | `transfer_fee`, `before` / `after`, `observed_at`, `previous_observed_at`) and `risk:supply_inflated` (level `warn` | `danger` at 0.5 % / 5 %, first crossing per level); `rhc:token_risk` event `rhc:risk_verdict_changed` (`changed`, `before` / `after` verdict, `flags_added` / `flags_removed`, `checked_at`, `previous_checked_at`, `detection`). These are changes of the risk INPUTS, never of the risk band or score, which moves with price and is not streamed (use GET /tokens/{mint}/risk). `slot` is null on the Solana events. The RHC score is higher = safer, the opposite of the Solana `risk_score`. RHC detection lag is NOT bounded to 24 h: the change happened somewhere in (`previous_checked_at`, `checked_at`], currently days to weeks apart (a full recheck cycle takes about 24 days, and only tokens with at least $500 liquidity are rechecked). On subscribe, on an `update` that changes the scope and on a resume, the server sends one state frame per token, `risk:inputs` / `rhc:risk_verdict` with `snapshot: true` and no id or seq; opt out with `filters.risk_snapshot: false`. Optional `filters.risk_events` narrows the event types. Ids `<event>:<event_key>`; durable resume from the event logs.

**Wallet scores.** `wallet:scores` events `deployer:tier_changed` (`tier_before`, `tier_after`, `entered_ranking`, `stats`) and `kol:score_state_changed` (only `is_cold`, `is_heating_up`, `auto_strategy_tag`); `rhc:wallet_scores` event `rhc:deployer_tier_changed`. `filters.wallets` is the scope key on BOTH chains (base58 wallets for Solana, 0x deployers for RHC; not `filters.addresses`, which means token addresses); optional `filters.score_events`. Every frame says when the value was RECOMPUTED, not when it changed: `source` `live_write` (a bond or deploy reclassified the deployer, real time), `scheduled_recompute` (the 6-hourly stats worker, the underlying stats can be hours older) or `matview_refresh` (the 10-minute KOL / 5-minute RHC recompute), with `computed_at` meaning that write, that run or that refresh. A Solana deployer entering a ranked tier from `unranked` counts as a tier change (`tier_before: unranked`, `entered_ranking: true`). No numeric or percentile score stream and no unscoped stream. Ids `<event>:<event_key>`; durable resume from the event logs.

User-scoped channels deliver only your own rule fires; the rest are broadcast.

**Event ids, sequence numbers, resume and replay (Phase 1, 2026-09-22).** Event frames carry `seq` and `id`; `token:price` ticks carry neither. `seq` is ONE ordinal per server process, shared by every channel and every customer and assigned before your filters run, so the seq values you receive have gaps in normal operation: **a gap is not evidence of loss**. `id` is stable: the same event has the same id live, re-sent from memory, rebuilt from storage or recovered after a bus reconnect, so delivery is **at-least-once; dedupe by `id`**. The `connected` frame carries the current `seq`, an `instance` id and the replay window.

**Resume.** Keep a cursor `{instance, seq, ts}` of the last frame your handler finished processing (it returned, or its promise settled) and reconnect with `{type:subscribe, channels, resume:{instance, seq, ts}}`. The `subscribed` ack echoes `resume` with `accepted: true` (`accepted: false`, `reason: replay_in_progress` plus a `warning` frame with that code when a replay is already running on the connection; its channels are still subscribed). Same instance and the cursor still inside the in-memory buffer (last 20,000 frames, about 6-8 minutes): frames are re-sent from memory (`mode: ring`, with their `seq`). Otherwise (server restart = `instance_changed`, or a longer absence = `ring_truncated`) each channel is rebuilt from storage from the cursor's `ts` (minus 60 s slack, deduped by id), bounded to **60 minutes, 2,000 rows per channel and 20,000 rows in total** (`rhc:dex_trades` / `rhc:dex_trades_unattributed`: 10 minutes back and up to 10,000 rows, which can include trades that were never pushed live). Rebuilt frames carry `seq: null`, `mode: durable`, `replayed: true`, and `partial: true` + `missing: [...]` where a field is not stored. `token:graduations` and `rhc:new_tokens` have no stored source: whatever the memory buffer holds is re-sent, then the channel reports gap `not_reconstructable`. `token:prices` gets the current price row per watched mint once (`snapshot: true`, `partial: true`). A resume or legacy replay is ALWAYS bracketed by `replay_start` and `replay_end`, even with nothing to replay. `replay_end` carries `sent`, `matched`, `complete`, `reason`, `retryable`, `retry_after_ms?`, `resume_ts_hint?`, `incomplete_channels?`, `last_seq`, `last_ts` (maxima over frames sent; `last_seq` never above `live_from_seq - 1`), `live_from_seq`, `mode`, `resume_reason`, `count` (legacy, equals `matched`) and `channels: {<channel>: {mode, sent, matched, complete, reason?, gap?, time_basis?, max_rows?, retryable?, retry_after_ms?, late_ingest_possible?, partial?, missing?, approximate?, since_ts?, truncated_at_ts?, gap_before_ts?}}`; reasons are `backpressure`, `instance_changed`, `ring_truncated`, `window_exceeded`, `row_cap`, `source_busy`, `source_error`, `late_ingest_possible`, `not_reconstructable`.

**Commit rule.** Replayed frames do not move your saved cursor (a storage replay is sent channel by channel, not in one time order). On `complete: true`, commit `{instance, seq: last_seq, ts: last_ts}` (keep your previous value where one is null) and let live frames advance it again. On `complete: false, retryable: true`, keep the cursor you resumed from and resume again after `retry_after_ms` (from `ts: resume_ts_hint` ONLY when the reply carries one — the server emits it when every incomplete RETRYABLE channel was cut by `row_cap` (a channel with a FINAL gap, such as `not_reconstructable` on `token:graduations` or `rhc:new_tokens`, does not block the hint, because retrying could not fetch anything behind it); with a mixed retryable set (say one `row_cap` and one `source_error` channel) there is no hint and you resume from your pre-resume cursor, because the hint would step past the failed channel's unread range. Per-channel `truncated_at_ts` is always present for a client that tracks channels separately); duplicates are dropped by id. On `complete: false, retryable: false` the reported gaps are final (`not_reconstructable`, `window_exceeded`, `ring_truncated`, `instance_changed`): backfill them from REST, then commit as for complete. SDK behaviour: on a retryable incomplete recovery our SDKs resume again on the same socket after `retry_after_ms` (up to `maxResumeRetries`, default 5), using `resume_ts_hint` only when every incomplete retryable channel is `row_cap`. The budget is per connection and its counter resets on every (re)connect. When that budget is spent, the gap event says `exhausted: true`: the client stops asking on that connection, the committed cursor stays where it is, and the next reconnect resumes again. On a FINAL gap they emit a gap event first (channels, reason, permanent, the server's bounds and the RANGE that may be incomplete as `skipped.from` -> `skipped.to`) with `advancedPastGap:true` and `source:"auto"`, then move the cursor past it. A count of missing events is never given because it cannot be known. That advance is the client library's own decision, not your approval: set `onUnrecoverableGap:"stop"` to keep the cursor instead, which stops the stream and emits fatal with the same gap, and `acceptGap()` then re-reports it with `source:"manual"` and continues. WATERMARK AND HOLDBACK: a row's id or timestamp is assigned when it is written, not when it commits, so a row with a lower id can still appear after a read passed it. The server therefore advances the committable watermark only across rows whose writing transaction had already finished when the read took its snapshot (xmin_blocked:true when it stops early), holds it 5 s behind now (holdback_ms) and re-scans the last 60 s (rescan_ms) on the next resume; a stuck long transaction cannot freeze it forever (capped at `maxHoldbackMs`, reported as `holdback_capped_ms`). While the cap is in force the channel reports `holdback_ms: 300000` (the nominal 5000 stays as `nominal_holdback_ms`) and its `guarantee` states the real bound and says `CAPPED`: about 6 minutes (5 min + the 60 s re-scan), not the usual 65 s. Frames are still delivered as they are read; the holdback only limits what you may commit, and last_ts is held to the tightest safe_ts (per channel in replay_end.channels.<ch>.watermark {scheme, safe_ts, holdback_ms, nominal_holdback_ms?, holdback_capped_ms?, rescan_ms, xmin_blocked, gate_ms?, guarantee}, overall in replay_end.watermark_safe_ts). RECOVERY IS BOUNDED, NOT A COMPLETENESS GUARANTEE: with the id and ingest-time schemes a write whose transaction commits more than about 65 s after its id or timestamp was taken can be missed (about 6 minutes instead while `holdback_capped_ms` is set), and for rhc:dex_trades / rhc:dex_trades_unattributed (scheme producer_gate) recovery is bounded by the producer's 600 s freshness rule, so a trade already older than 600 s when it was ingested is not recoverable through this path at all. Each channel states its own bound in watermark.guarantee. **Late writes:** every storage read pages by an ingest-time column, a storage id or the producer's own freshness window, so a row written late is not skipped; a channel that could not rule that out would report `complete: false`, `reason: late_ingest_possible`, never `complete: true`. **Load:** recovery is limited server-wide; a resume waits up to 20 s for a slot, otherwise its storage-backed channels report `source_busy` with `retry_after_ms` (memory frames are still sent). A second replay request while one is still running gets only a `replay_in_progress` warning, no second `replay_start` / `replay_end`. Live frames that arrive during a replay are held (up to 5,000 frames or 4 MB per socket, counting each subscription's copy of a frame, so N overlapping named subscriptions use N slots per event; price ticks coalesced per mint and subscription) and delivered after `replay_end`, skipping ids already sent. A socket that cannot drain during a replay gets `complete: false`, `reason: backpressure` and a 4008 close; reconnect and resume. Frames can only be lost across a disconnect or a 4008 close, and the resume reply states what was and was not recovered. **Legacy:** `replay_since_seq` / `replay_since_ts` still work, from memory only; `replay_start` now reports `replay_truncated: true` with `reason` `instance_changed` or `ring_truncated` instead of replaying nothing silently. If the server's own event-bus connection drops, missed events are re-read from storage (up to 60 minutes, 5,000 rows per channel, 10,000 for the RHC DEX trade channels) and delivered with `replayed: true`, `recovered: bus`.

**Entitlements.** Every frame is checked against your current plan; after a downgrade, channels above it are dropped with a `warning` frame `code: channels_revoked` (also a `token:prices` mint set above the new cap). Revoking or rotating your API key deletes the stream token: open sockets close with 4001 within about a minute; mint a new one with the new key. Heartbeat pings every 15 s. Connection slots: PRO 2 · ULTRA 5 · BUSINESS 15 (see /stream/sessions to list or evict a slot).

**Named subscriptions (Phase 2).** A subscribe without `sub_id` is the connection's implicit `default` subscription: one channel set and one filter object for the whole socket (`action: "buy"` on it also drops `deployer:alerts`, whose payload has no action), exactly as before. A subscribe carrying `sub_id` (1-64 characters of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ . -`) opens or extends an independent subscription with its OWN channels and filters: `{type:subscribe, sub_id, channels, filters}` is acked `subscribed {sub_id, channels, filters, seq, instance, resume?}`, `{type:update, sub_id, filters}` REPLACES that subscription's filters (`updated {sub_id, filters}`), `{type:unsubscribe, sub_id}` removes it (`unsubscribed {sub_id}`; with `channels` it drops only those; a bare `{type:unsubscribe}` still clears every subscription and now acks `unsubscribed {channels: [], all: true}`), and `{type:list}` answers `subscriptions {list:[{sub_id, channels, filters}], count, max}`. Every frame delivered under a named subscription carries `sub_id`; the default subscription's frames carry none. **An event that matches several subscriptions is delivered once per matching subscription**, each copy stamped with its `sub_id`, so dedupe by `(sub_id, id)`. Filters of one subscription never affect another; tier gates, user scoping and revocation apply per subscription (`channels_revoked` names the `sub_id`). Refusals are `warning` frames with the `sub_id` and one of `invalid_sub_id`, `too_many_subscriptions`, `unknown_sub_id`, `invalid_filters`, `channels_rejected`, `replay_in_progress`. The cap counts every subscription on the connection, the default one included: **PRO 5 · ULTRA 10 · BUSINESS 20** (`named_subscriptions.max_per_connection` in this response). `token:prices` mints are capped per CONNECTION across all subscriptions. Resume is per subscription: a subscribe with `sub_id` and `resume` replays only that subscription's channels through its own filters (its `replay_start` / `replay_end` carry the `sub_id`); a client holding several subscriptions re-sends each of them with the SAME cursor on reconnect, the server serves the replays one after another (`resume.queued: true` on the acks that wait; a repeat request for a sub_id that already has one running or queued is refused `replay_in_progress`) and holds live frames until the last `replay_end`; commit the cursor only after the last one, at the smallest `last_seq` / `last_ts` across them. The cursor itself stays per connection (`seq` / `ts` are global).

200.description: OK — { token, ws_url, expires_at: null, next_refresh_at: null, rotated, lifetime, dex_ws_url?, channels[], token_prices: { ... }, named_subscriptions: { ... } }

expires_at.description: Always null — tokens do not expire, kept for wire compatibility

rotated.description: true when this call replaced a previous token (rotate:true was sent, or an existing token was minted fresh)

lifetime.description: Human-readable explanation of the non-expiring token lifecycle

early_ws_url.description: Present only for ULTRA/BUSINESS/ENTERPRISE when ShredPrism is activated. Use the same stream token at this separate early gateway.

early_stream.description: Activation-gated ShredPrism early-stream discovery for ULTRA/BUSINESS/ENTERPRISE. Only implemented channels are advertised. Full wire contract: /docs/shredprism-stream.md and machine-readable channel schemas: /api/v1/asyncapi.json. Subscriptions support wallet/token/label filters, directions and exact raw instruction-amount rules plus opt-in lossless compact-v1 JSON; full JSON remains the default.

coverage.description: Supported outer-instruction scope and intent-only amount semantics.

dex_ws_url.description: Present for ULTRA/BUSINESS only — the DEX firehose socket (wss://madeonsol.com/ws/v1/dex-stream). Frames: `dex:trades` (one normalized trade per transaction, the signer's net effect; dedupe by tx_signature), in-band `dex:graduations` on mint-scoped subscriptions, and, since 2026-09-22, the opt-in per-pool view: subscribe with `legs: true` (or `"only"`) to receive per transaction one `dex:route` {signature, slot, signer, hop_count, leg_ids[], shape, decoded_complete, undecoded_program_ids[], liquidity_actions[], router_program, signer_net[], trade_mint} and one `dex:leg` per decoded pool swap {leg_id = `<signature>:<instruction_index>[.<inner_index>][#h<k>]` (stable live and on replay; `#h<k>` marks hop k >= 1 of ONE multi-hop instruction, which yields one leg per pool, those legs also carry hop_index and instruction_hop_count), program, venue, pool_model, pool, pool_kind, pool_authority, vault_in, vault_out, token_in/token_out {mint, amount_raw (integer string), decimals, amount_ui, native}, side, amount_basis, is_route_member; a leg decoded from a liquidity instruction whose balances read as a swap, e.g. Meteora DLMM rebalance_liquidity, also carries liquidity_instruction (the instruction name) and liquidity_instruction_kind (add | remove | create | migrate | rebalance): a liquidity position change, not a trade, so exclude it from trade analyses; normal swap legs carry neither key}, followed by the unchanged `dex:trades` frame exactly once (omitted with `legs: "only"`). Liquidity deposits/withdrawals are never a leg (listed on the route). The `subscribed` ack of a legs subscription carries `coverage.decodable_programs`; a route touching a program we do not decode says `decoded_complete: false` and names it. **Liquidity events (2026-09-23):** subscribe with `liquidity: true` (in addition to trades) or `"only"` (liquidity frames only; cannot be combined with `legs`) to receive `dex:liquidity` {id = `<signature>:<ix>[.<inner>]`, action pool_created | add | remove, program, venue, instruction, pool, pool_kind, pool_model, mints[{mint, amount_raw, decimals, side in|out}], lp_mint, owner, signer, amount_basis, reserves_before[] / reserves_after[] (raw vault balances), share_of_reserves (constant-product only), depth_effect, material (a removal of at least 25 % of reserves)}. Filters per subscription: token_mint(s), wallet(s), pool(s), dex, program (one of them is required with `"only"`), actions, min_share_of_reserves, material_only. Only liquidity instructions proven by a real transaction fixture are emitted (listed with `emits_events` in the ack's `liquidity_coverage`); other recognised ones appear on the route as `event: false`. Concentrated pools (CLMM, Whirlpool, DLMM) report share and depth as unknown; Meteora DAMM v1, Raydium LaunchLab and Moonshot are not emitted; there is no USD field and `min_usd` is rejected. Replay from the in-memory ring only; no durable resume (`not_reconstructable`). Full protocol in docs/api.md § DEX Firehose.

get.summary: Bulk Parquet exports of archived months (BUSINESS+)
get.description:
BUSINESS+ (BASIC/PRO/ULTRA get 403 with an `upgrade` block; ENTERPRISE passes). Two modes on one route.

**Listing** (no params): every fully archived closed month per dataset — `token_trades`, `rhc_trades`, `token_ohlc_1m`, `rhc_ohlc_1m` — with row count, byte size and file count. A month appears only once both archive providers have verified it (the same ledger the nightly archive exporter writes), so the list is the set you can actually download.

**Download** (`dataset` + `month`): presigned S3 GET links for that month's Parquet files (zstd-compressed, one or more files per month). Links are valid for about **1 hour** — fetch them when you are ready to download, not ahead of time; re-request to mint fresh ones. The ledger row count is returned so you can verify the files you pulled. Both params are required together.

The current (open) month is never listed — it is live in Postgres and served by the paginated endpoints (`/tokens/{mint}/trades`, `/rhc/trades`, `/tokens/{mint}/candles`). Files are identical to the immutable dual-provider archive described at https://madeonsol.com/data-integrity — ideal for backtests, model training and offline analytics without paging through the API.

get.summary: New vs returning buyers per 5 minutes (PRO+)
get.description: Distinct buyer wallets of a Solana memecoin per 5-minute bucket (epoch-aligned, ingest clock), split into `returning` (an earlier stored buy of this mint exists), `seen_before_as_seller_only` (no earlier stored buy, but an earlier stored sell of this mint), `new` (no earlier stored buy or sell, and the mint's history is provable) and `undetermined` (no earlier stored buy, but the history needed to say new is not provable; every undetermined wallet has a reason). `new` is never "first ever": it is relative to the rows we stored. It is provable only when the launch is recorded inside the Postgres months (`history.postgres_floor`; the Parquet archive is not read), our first stored trade is within 15 minutes of the launch, the launch is after the zero-floor boundary (before 2026-10-22 19:52:45 UTC buys under 0.05 SOL / $3.50 were not stored, `size_floor_periods`), and no unrecovered capture gap lies between the launch and the bucket. `history.complete_from` is the earliest stored trade of the mint and `history.predates_window` says whether it is before the window. `coverage_summary` lists the capture gaps checked, the unattributed buy rows, the trader-unproven buyers and every undetermined reason in the window. buyers = new + returning + seen_before_as_seller_only + undetermined when new_buyers is a number; returning + undetermined when it is null.

200.description: Buckets oldest first; the last bucket is partial.

complete_from.description: Earliest stored trade of the mint.

unattributed_buy_rows.description: Buy rows in the window whose trader is not proven (not counted as buyers).

trader_unproven_buyers.description: Buyers in the window whose only earlier buys are rows with an unproven trader (undetermined).

capture_gaps.description: Unrecovered capture gaps read for this response (from the launch when it is at most 40 days old, else the window start).

status.description: gap_overlap / gap_unverified: a recorded capture gap overlaps the bucket (or its bounds are unknown), so buyers is a lower bound. not_captured: every count is null.

buyers.description: Distinct wallets with a buy in the bucket whose trader is proven (trader_status null, signer or non_signer).

new_buyers.description: No earlier stored buy or sell of this mint and the history is provable. Null (with null_reasons.new_buyers) when it is not; those wallets are in undetermined_buyers.

returning_buyers.description: An earlier stored buy of this mint exists (earlier in the window or before it).

seen_before_as_seller_only.description: No earlier stored buy of this mint, but an earlier stored sell by the same wallet (its own trade): neither returning nor new. Null (with null_reasons.seen_before_as_seller_only) when the history is not provable, because an earlier buy could be missing from our rows; those wallets are in undetermined_buyers.

undetermined_buyers.description: Wallets without an earlier stored buy that cannot be called new; undetermined_reasons breaks them down.

undetermined_reasons.description: Count per reason: launch_not_recorded, before_capture, capture_start_unproven, capture_unverified, size_floor, capture_gap, trader_unproven.

unattributed_buy_rows.description: Buy rows in the bucket whose trader is not proven (not counted as buyers).

429.description: Rate, daily or heavy-query limit reached.

503.description: The token has too many buyers to classify inside the statement budget; retry or use a shorter window.
